open_decisions.question: Copybook SQLCA (src/copybook/db2/SQLCA.cpy) includes itself (EXEC SQL INCLUDE SQLCA at line 6) and defines only SQL-STATUS-CODES, with no SQLCODE or SQLERRMC field; SQLCODE/SQLERRMC therefore have no Field ID in 14 DB2 programs, including HISTLD00, RTNANA00, RTNCDE00, DB2CMT and DB2CONN. Which SQLCA does the precompiler actually supply, and may the forward design assume the standard DB2 SQLCODE meaning (0 success, -803 duplicate key, negative values errors) used in these requirements?

DB2ERR (line 75) uses the non-standard 'ACCEPT WS-CURRENT-TIMESTAMP FROM TIME STAMP'; the ERRPROC logic file flags the same construct (line 57) and PORTDEL uses it for the deletion audit timestamp (source line 169). Which compiler extension is in use and what timestamp format do ERRLOG rows, error-log records and deletion audit records actually carry?

HISTLD00 moves 13 TH-* fields (TH-ACCOUNT-NO ... TH-GAIN-LOSS) to POSHIST-RECORD and updates BCT-RECORDS-READ / BCT-RECORDS-WRITTEN, but none of these names is declared in HISTREC or BCHCTL as registered. What is the transaction-history record layout actually read by HISTLD00, and where are the checkpoint counters stored?

Fifteen elementary level-01 items (e.g. HISTLD00 WS-COMMIT-THRESHOLD, the REPORT-RECORD print lines, DB2CONN WS-CONNECTION-STATE/WS-RETRY-COUNT/WS-MAX-RETRIES, DB2CMT WS-SAVEPOINT-ID) are catalogued as record-level items without Field IDs, so no Java type could be assigned. Should the reverse harness register Field IDs for them, or may later stages map them at record level using the catalogued PIC?

HISTLD00 performs CONNECT-TO-DB2, DB2-ERROR-ROUTINE and DISCONNECT-FROM-DB2, which are not registered for the program (expected from COPY DBPROC), and has no restart repositioning (a rerun relies on SQLCODE -803). Should the Java job use container-managed connections and a restartable reader keyed on the checkpoint counters, or reproduce the rerun-from-start behaviour?

DD TRANHIST is declared as TRANSACTION-HISTORY in HISTLD00 (RECORD KEY TH-KEY, copybook HISTREC) and in RPTPOS00 (RECORD KEY TRAN-KEY, copybook TRNREC). Do both programs address the same indexed dataset, and which key/record layout is authoritative?

The character encoding of DISPLAY data is not stated anywhere (source declares IBM-ZOS only). Is EBCDIC code page 037 correct for all files and the DB2 subsystem, or another code page (e.g. 1140 with the euro sign, which changes the '$' currency byte in WS-POS-VALUE)?

Copybook SQLCA (SYS-PORTFOLIO-001-FIL-0017) line 6 contains 'EXEC SQL INCLUDE SQLCA END-EXEC', naming itself. The included SQL communication area (SQLCODE, SQLSTATE, SQLERRMC, ...) has no layout in any reverse artifact. How should the forward design obtain the SQLCA layout and the SQLCODE/SQLSTATE semantics used by the 14 DB2 programs?

DBPROC procedure code (DB2-ERROR-ROUTINE, lines 47-56) moves data to ERR-PROGRAM and ERR-TEXT and calls 'ERRPROC' USING ERR-MESSAGE, but DBPROC declares none of these and ERR-TEXT is declared in no packet copybook. Which record declares ERR-TEXT / ERR-MESSAGE in each including program, and what is the ERRPROC parameter layout?

Which TRUNC compiler option (STD, OPT or BIN) was used for programs including these copybooks? It decides whether S9(4)/S9(8)/S9(9) COMP fields are truncated to their PIC digits or to the binary halfword/fullword range on store.

ERRPROC's LINKAGE LS-ERROR-REQUEST is 354 bytes, but DB2ERR (line 199) and DB2STAT (line 227) CALL 'ERRPROC' USING ERR-MESSAGE from copybook ERRHAND (about 370 bytes, different field order). Which layout is the contract of the Java error service?

BCHCON BCT-EMERGENCY is PIC X(8) with VALUE 'EMERGENCY' (9 characters). What initial 8-byte value must the Java constant hold: the compiler-truncated 'EMERGENC', or is the copybook to be corrected (for example a 9-byte field or a different literal)?

Which character encoding (code page) do the files and areas described by these copybooks use for DISPLAY data on the legacy platform (EBCDIC 037, 1140, another EBCDIC variant, or ASCII)? The zoned-decimal test vectors and String codecs depend on it.

Which TRUNC compiler option (STD, OPT or BIN) were the programs including these copybooks compiled with? It decides whether COMP fields such as 9(2) COMP, 9(3) COMP, 9(5) COMP and 9(9) COMP may hold values beyond their PIC digits (up to the halfword/fullword limit), which affects Java range validation and whether 9(9) COMP counters need long instead of int.

HISTLD00 performs CONNECT-TO-DB2, DB2-ERROR-ROUTINE and DISCONNECT-FROM-DB2, which exist only as procedure code in copybook DBPROC (lines 26-63) and were not traced. What do the DB2 connect, the DB2 error routine (called for every non-duplicate POSHIST insert failure) and the disconnect do, and does the error routine change the flow of the load (for example rollback or stop)?

HISTLD00 moves 13 history source fields (TH-ACCOUNT-NO, TH-PORTFOLIO-ID, TH-TRANS-DATE, TH-TRANS-TIME, TH-TRANS-TYPE, TH-SECURITY-ID, TH-QUANTITY, TH-PRICE, TH-AMOUNT, TH-FEES, TH-TOTAL-AMOUNT, TH-COST-BASIS, TH-GAIN-LOSS; lines 146-158) into POSHIST and two checkpoint counters (BCT-RECORDS-READ, BCT-RECORDS-WRITTEN; lines 192-193) into the batch-control record, but none of them is declared in the program or its copybooks. What are the real record layouts of the transaction-history input and of the batch-control checkpoint fields?

BR-007 states: at every commit the running totals of records read and records written are copied into the batch-control record (BCT-RECORDS-READ, BCT-RECORDS-WRITTEN) and the record is rewritten; the commit counter restarts at zero. The two target fields are not declared in BATCH-CONTROL-RECORD. Confirm, correct or reject: where must the checkpoint totals be stored, and are they used for restart?

BR-005 describes the commit threshold (1000) as 'records loaded since the last commit', but HISTLD00 adds 1 to the commit counter for every history record processed, including duplicate-key rows (SQLCODE -803, counted neither as written nor as error) and failed inserts. BR-006 (per-record counters) is medium confidence. Is the commit interval meant to count every processed record (as the source does) or only successfully loaded records, and are the read/written/error counting rules correct?

Copybook HISTREC declares history record types HIST-RECORD-TYPE ('PT' portfolio, 'PS' position, 'TR' transaction; BR-146) and actions HIST-ACTION-CODE ('A' add, 'C' change, 'D' delete; BR-147); HISTLD00 does not test them. Must the forward history load validate or route on these values?
